mainTopic: Using found money, caring for found scrolls, garments and vessels, borrowed and deposited Torah scrolls, and רבי יוחנן's practical advice
overview: The גמרא finishes the earlier משנה by quoting רבה: a finder who is allowed to use the money must pay even if it is taken by armed bandits or lost in a shipwreck. It rules like רבי טרפון, but אביי shows that the permission covers only money a finder earned by caring for a lost object, so רחבה may not use orphans' money. A new משנה then explains how a finder looks after scrolls, garments and vessels, and when he need not pick up an item at all. שמואל rules that found תפילין may be valued and the money set aside, because new תפילין are easy to buy while scrolls are not. A ברייתא gives rules for a borrowed or deposited ספר תורה, and the גמרא explains each line, correcting the view of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. Next come a contradiction about two people reading one scroll and four answers about whether shaking a garment helps it. The amud ends with practical advice from רבי יוחנן about lukewarm water and about habits that waste an inheritance. The explanation of the last habit continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Explaining 'stolen' and 'lost' through רבה's definition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers its earlier question by reading the משנה's words 'stolen' and 'lost' the way רבה does: armed robbers and a sunken ship.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows רבה, who said: 'stolen' means taken by armed bandits, and 'lost' means his ship sank at sea.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a question from just before this point about the משנה's ruling on money that went missing. It uses רבה's definition of the words 'stolen' and 'lost.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that, because the finder may use the money, he must pay if it is lost. רבה's definition shows what this adds: he must pay even for אונס, losses nobody could prevent, like armed robbers or a shipwreck. Being allowed to use the money puts him in a stricter category of responsibility.

keyTerms.meaning: Armed bandits, a robbery no guardian could stop
An unavoidable accident, beyond a person's control

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'lost' here as 'he misplaced it.' רבה means a disaster beyond his control, like a sunken ship.

phrases.english: In accordance with Rabba.
As Rabba said:
'They were stolen' means by armed bandits;
'They were lost' means that his ship sank at sea.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised just before this point about the משנה's wording
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the משנה's words as cases of אונס
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Stolen' and 'lost' sound like ordinary losses a guardian should prevent
steps.terutzMaskana: Even for armed robbery and shipwreck, losses no one could prevent, he must pay, because he was allowed to use the money

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי טרפון
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting שמואל, rules like רבי טרפון: the finder may use money from selling a lost object.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי טרפון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a final ruling on the dispute in the משנה. The halacha follows רבי טרפון, who lets the finder use the money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה had a dispute about using money from selling a lost object. This ruling picks רבי טרפון's side. The story that follows will test how far this permission goes.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical ruling, and the next steps will narrow its scope.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halacha is in accordance with Rabbi Tarfon.
phrases.notes: רבי טרפון is the one in the משנה who allowed the finder to use the money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי טַרְפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining the משנה to ruling on its dispute
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The finder may use money from the sale of a lost object, as רבי טרפון holds

steps.title: רחבה asks about using orphans' money
steps.stepSummary: רחבה was holding money that belonged to orphans and asked רב יוסף whether he could use it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רחבה had some money belonging to orphans. He came to רב יוסף and asked: may I use it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that sets up a real-life test of the ruling. רחבה asks whether he can use the orphans' money in his care.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether רבי טרפון's permission reaches other money a person is holding for someone else. Orphans' money is kept safe for owners who cannot claim it yet, so it looks somewhat like found money.

phrases.english: In the possession of Rachava there were
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets; the corrected wording uses the word in square brackets. The meaning is the same.

phrases.english: these dinars belonging to orphans.
He came before Rav Yosef.
He said to him: What is the law about using them?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּיַד רַחֲבָה הֲווֹ הָנְהוּ זוּזֵי דְיַתְמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ruling of step 2 to a real case
steps.sheelahInformationSought: May a person holding orphans' money use it?

steps.title: רב יוסף permits it based on רבי טרפון
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers by quoting the ruling that the halacha follows רבי טרפון, which suggests רחבה may use the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: this is what רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי טרפון.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers רחבה by quoting the ruling from step 2. He means: yes, you may use the money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף treats the orphans' money like the money in the משנה. Since the halacha follows רבי טרפון, he allows its use.

phrases.english: He said to him: This is what
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halacha is in accordance with Rabbi Tarfon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָכִי אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רחבה's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, he may use it, because the halacha follows רבי טרפון

steps.title: אביי: the permission only covers money the finder worked for
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects that רבי טרפון's permission only applies to money from selling a lost object the finder cared for. It does not apply to coins that were simply found, and orphans' money is like found coins.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Wasn't it said about this, in the name of רבי חלבו quoting רב הונא, that the rule only applies to דמי אבידה, since he put work into it? Found coins, where he put in no work, may not be used. And this money is like found coins.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב יוסף's answer. He quotes a teaching that limits רבי טרפון's permission to cases where the finder worked to care for the lost object.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The finder of an object has to feed it or care for it and then sell it, so the rabbis let him use the money as a reward for his effort. Someone who just finds coins made no effort, so he gets no permission. רחבה made no special effort with the orphans' money either, so he cannot use it.

keyTerms.meaning: Money from selling a lost object
Lost coins found as they are

steps.confusionAlert: Both cases involve money, but they are different. דמי אבידה is money the finder got by working on an object. מעות אבידה are coins he simply picked up.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the real limit of רבי טרפון's ruling: the permission to use the money depends on the finder's effort.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But wasn't it stated about it

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Chelbo said that Rav Huna said:
They taught this only about money from a lost object,
since he exerted himself with it;
but lost coins,
where he did not exert himself with them, no.
And these are like lost coins.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי וְלָאו אִתְּמַר עֲלַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's permission in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's use of רבי טרפון's ruling to allow use of the orphans' money
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The permission is a reward for the finder's effort, and no such effort was made with the orphans' money

steps.title: רב יוסף withdraws his permission
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף accepts אביי's objection and tells רחבה he cannot permit him to use the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Go, they did not let me permit it to you.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף accepts אביי's objection and takes back his answer. רחבה may not use the orphans' money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'They did not let me' means אביי's objection showed the permission does not fit this case. The final outcome is that the orphans' money must stay untouched.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי טרפון allows using money only when the finder worked on the lost object. Found coins and orphans' money may not be used.

phrases.english: He said to him: Go;
they did not let me permit it to you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ זִיל לָא שְׁבַקוּ לִי דְּאֶשְׁרֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the objection of step 5
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The orphans' money may not be used, because it is like found coins

steps.title: New משנה: caring for found scrolls
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that a finder of ספרים must read them once every thirty days, or roll them if he can't read. He may not study new material in them, and another person may not read along with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone found scrolls, he reads them once every thirty days. If he does not know how to read, he rolls them. But he may not study them for the first time, and another person may not read with him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, explaining how a finder should look after found ספרים until the owner comes. He must air them regularly without harming them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading the scrolls once a month keeps them aired and in good condition, and rolling them does the same job. Studying something new takes too long, and two readers might pull at the scroll, so both are forbidden because they could damage it.

keyTerms.meaning: For the first time, new material

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If one found scrolls,
he reads them once in thirty days.
And if he does not know how to read, he rolls them.
But he may not study in them for the first time,
and another may not read with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָצָא סְפָרִים קוֹרֵא בָּהֶן אֶחָד לִשְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: caring for found ספרים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A finder airs found scrolls once every thirty days, but may not study new material in them or read together with someone else

steps.title: Caring for a found garment
steps.stepSummary: A finder of a garment shakes it out once every thirty days and spreads it out for its own good, but not to show it off for his own honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he found a garment, he shakes it out once every thirty days and spreads it out for its own needs, but not for his own honor.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of found items and now rules on a found garment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Clothing that sits folded for a long time gets ruined, so the finder must air it out. That care is for the garment's sake only. He may not use it to make himself look good.

keyTerms.meaning: A garment, a piece of clothing
For his own honor or prestige

phrases.english: If he found a garment
he shakes it out once every thirty days
and spreads it out for its own needs
but not for his own honor.
phrases.notes: He can air it out, but he can't use it to show off or decorate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of found items, moving from ספרים to clothing
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A finder airs out a found garment every thirty days for its sake, never for his own prestige.

steps.title: Using found silver and copper vessels
steps.stepSummary: Found silver and copper vessels may be used for their own good, but not so much that they wear down.
steps.simpleTranslation: Silver vessels and copper vessels: he uses them for their own needs, but not to the point of wearing them out.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה rules on found metal vessels that can be damaged by sitting unused.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the finder is actually allowed to use the item, because light use protects it. Heavy use that grinds the metal down is forbidden, since that harms the owner.

keyTerms.meaning: For their own needs, for the vessels' good

phrases.english: Silver vessels and copper vessels
he uses them for their own needs
but not to wear them out.
phrases.notes: Literally 'to grind them down,' meaning using them so much that the metal wears away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the משנה's list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Silver and copper vessels may be used lightly for their own good, but not worn down.

steps.title: Gold and glass vessels are left untouched
steps.stepSummary: Found gold and glass vessels may not be touched at all; the finder simply holds them indefinitely.
steps.simpleTranslation: Gold vessels and glass vessels: he may not touch them until אליהו comes.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה rules that found gold and glass vessels must be left alone completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike silver and copper, these items don't get ruined by sitting, so there is no reason to use them. Using them would only create risk, so the finder just keeps them safe for as long as it takes.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Until אליהו comes' doesn't mean the finder is waiting for a miracle. It means he keeps the item untouched for as long as it takes, with no end date.

phrases.english: Gold vessels and glass vessels
he may not touch them
until אליהו comes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with silver and copper vessels: these may not be used at all
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gold and glass vessels may not be touched; they are held indefinitely for the owner.

steps.title: Items beneath the finder's dignity
steps.stepSummary: If the found item is something the finder would never normally carry, such as a sack or basket, he does not have to take it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he found a sack or a basket, or any item that he would not normally carry, he does not take it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with an exception: some lost items the finder does not need to pick up at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The duty to return lost objects normally applies to these items too. But a person whose dignity would be lowered by carrying such things is not required to pick them up. The yardstick is the finder's own normal behavior.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not his normal way to carry it

steps.whatToRemember: The finder must care for each item according to what that item needs. And if carrying it is beneath him, he need not take it at all.

phrases.english: If he found a sack or a basket
or any item that he would not normally take
phrases.notes: 'His way' means this particular person: someone who would feel it beneath him to be seen carrying it.

phrases.english: he should not take it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the משנה with an exemption from picking up certain items
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One need not take a lost item that it is beneath his dignity to carry.

steps.title: שמואל: Found תפילין may be valued and the money set aside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with שמואל's ruling: one who finds תפילין assesses their value and immediately sets the money aside for the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: שמואל said: One who finds תפילין in the marketplace assesses their value and sets it aside immediately.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a new statement from שמואל about found תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With found ספרים (step 7), the finder must hold them and keep them in good shape. With תפילין, שמואל says the finder doesn't have to wait: he can fix their value right away and keep the money for the owner instead. This sets up a contrast the גמרא will now explore.

keyTerms.meaning: תפילין, the boxes worn on the head and arm

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that some found items do not have to be held for the owner at all. The owner may be just as happy with the money.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Shmuel said:
One who finds תפילין in the marketplace
assesses their value
and sets them aside immediately.
phrases.notes: 'Them' here is the money: he sets the value aside for the owner right away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא on the משנה, opening a discussion that contrasts with the משנה's rule for found ספרים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A finder of תפילין may value them and set aside the money immediately rather than holding the תפילין.

steps.title: רבינא's challenge from found scrolls
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges שמואל from the משנה: found scrolls are only rolled, not sold, so why should found תפילין be sold?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא objects: the משנה says one who finds scrolls reads them once every thirty days, and if he can't read, he rolls them. That means rolling, yes, but valuing them and setting the money aside, no. So how can שמואל say that found תפילין are valued and the money set aside?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא quotes our משנה about found scrolls to attack שמואל's ruling that found תפילין may be valued and the money set aside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה tells the finder to look after the scrolls by rolling them, and it says nothing about selling them. רבינא reads this as a clear 'no' to selling. Since תפילין are also holy writings, they should seem to follow the same rule, which goes against שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: he rolls them (to air them out)

phrases.english: Ravina raises an objection:
If he found scrolls, he reads them
once in thirty days;
and if he does not know how to read, he rolls them.
Rolling them, yes;
assessing their value and setting it aside, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks שמואל's ruling from Step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that found תפילין are valued and the money set aside
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה only allows rolling found scrolls, which implies they may not be sold. Holy writings like תפילין should be treated the same way.

steps.title: תפילין are easy to replace, scrolls are not
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that תפילין can easily be bought again, so selling them is no loss to the owner, but scrolls are hard to find.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: תפילין are readily available at the house of בר חבו, but scrolls are not readily available.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends שמואל by showing a real difference between תפילין and scrolls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner of lost תפילין loses nothing if he gets money back, because he can easily buy new ones. A scroll is rare and hard to replace, so the finder must keep the actual scroll for the owner. The two rulings are about different cases and do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: the house of בר חבו, a place with plenty of תפילין

steps.whatToRemember: Found תפילין may be valued and the money set aside because they are easy to replace. Found scrolls must be kept and looked after because they are hard to get.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Tefillin, at the house of Bar Chavu,
phrases.notes: בר חבו's house had plenty of תפילין, so the owner can easily buy a new pair with the money.

phrases.english: are readily available;
scrolls are not available.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: תְּפִילִּין בֵּי בַּר חָבוּ מִשְׁכָּח שְׁכִיחִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's challenge from Step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (תפילין are replaceable, scrolls are not)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All holy writings follow one rule, so תפילין should be kept and not sold, like scrolls.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because תפילין are easy to buy, money serves the owner just as well. Scrolls are rare, so they must be kept.

steps.title: Rules for borrowing a Torah scroll
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a borrower of a ספר תורה may not lend it out, and may read it only in a careful way.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: one who borrows a ספר תורה from his friend may not lend it to someone else. He may open it and read it, as long as he does not study new material in it for the first time, and no one else reads together with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: a ברייתא listing the rules for someone who borrowed a ספר תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The borrower may use the scroll for normal reading, since that is why he borrowed it. He must avoid uses that could harm it, such as keeping it open for a long time to learn something new, or having two people handle it at once.

keyTerms.meaning: may not lend it to someone else
for the first time (learning something new)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who borrows a Torah scroll from his friend,
may not lend it to another.
He may open it and read in it,
provided that he does not study in it for the first time,
and another person shall not read with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַשּׁוֹאֵל סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה מֵחֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא, related to the topic of handling scrolls
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A borrower of a ספר תורה may not lend it out. He may read it, but not learn new material in it, and no second person may read with him.

steps.title: Rules for a Torah scroll left for safekeeping
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: one guarding a deposited ספר תורה rolls it every twelve months, but may not open it for his own use.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly, if someone deposits a ספר תורה with his friend, the friend rolls it every twelve months. He opens it and reads in it. If he opened it for his own sake, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves from a borrower to a שומר who is holding someone's ספר תורה for safekeeping.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rolling the scroll once a year is good for the scroll, so the שומר does it for the owner. He may read while rolling, since that is part of airing it out. Opening it only because he wants to use it is forbidden, because he was not given permission to use it.

keyTerms.meaning: one who deposits an item with a guardian

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. A borrower was given the scroll to use, so he may read it. A שומר was only asked to guard it, so he may open it only for the scroll's own good.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הַמַּפְקִיד סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה אֵצֶל חֲבֵירוֹ,
phrases.english: And similarly, one who deposits a Torah scroll with his friend,
he rolls it every twelve months;
he opens it and reads in it.
If he opened it for himself, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן הַמַּפְקִיד סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה אֵצֶל חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a new case: a deposit instead of a loan
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A guardian of a deposited ספר תורה rolls it every twelve months and may read while doing so, but may not open it for his own benefit.

steps.title: How often to roll a new or old scroll
steps.stepSummary: סומכוס says a new scroll is rolled every thirty days and an old one every twelve months. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says both are rolled every twelve months.
steps.simpleTranslation: סומכוס says: a new scroll every thirty days, an old scroll every twelve months. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: both of them, every twelve months.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a dispute about how often a deposited scroll must be rolled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סומכוס splits the case: a new scroll needs airing more often, so every thirty days. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב makes no difference between them and says twelve months for both.

keyTerms.meaning: both this one and that one

phrases.english: Sumchus says:
For a new one, thirty days;
for an old one, twelve months.
Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה – שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ.
phrases.english: Both this and that, twelve months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a dispute about the rolling schedule from Step 16
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סומכוס: a new scroll is rolled every thirty days and an old one every twelve months. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: every twelve months for both.

steps.title: Why mention a Torah scroll specifically
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא says a borrowed ספר תורה may not be lent out, since ריש לקיש says no borrowed item may be lent out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: one who borrows a ספר תורה from his friend may not lend it to someone else. Why specifically a ספר תורה? The same is true of anything, as רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: here רבי taught that a borrower may not lend, and a renter may not rent out!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the first line of the ברייתא and asks why it needed to mention a ספר תורה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש shows that a משנה already teaches a general rule: nothing borrowed may be lent out, and nothing rented may be rented out. If so, singling out a ספר תורה seems to add nothing. The גמרא is now setting up the search for what this ברייתא teaches that is new.

phrases.english: The Master said:
One who borrows a Torah scroll from his friend
may not lend it to another.
Why specifically a Torah scroll?
The same is true even of all things,
as Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
Here Rebbi taught:
phrases.notes: 'Here' points to a משנה in גיטין 29a, which רבי יהודה הנשיא arranged.

phrases.english: A borrower is not allowed to lend,
and a renter is not allowed to rent out!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִרְיָא סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה? אֲפִילּוּ כֹּל מִילֵּי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the opening line of the ברייתא in Step 15 and questions it
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's mention of ספר תורה in the rule against lending out a borrowed item
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ריש לקיש shows that a משנה already forbids lending out any borrowed item, so naming a ספר תורה seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Why the ספר תורה case had to be stated
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא had to mention a ספר תורה specifically. Otherwise we might think the owner is happy to have a מצוה done with his property, so lending it on would be allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary to mention a ספר תורה. You might have said that a person is glad to have a מצוה done with his property, so he would not mind if it were lent to someone else. The ברייתא teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 18. Why does the ברייתא say a borrowed ספר תורה may not be lent out, if ריש לקיש already says this about every borrowed item?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ספר תורה looks like a special case. Lending it lets someone else learn Torah, so we might assume the owner would agree. The ברייתא tells us the general rule still applies: the borrower may not lend it out without the owner's permission.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary for him (to say this)
You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)
He is pleased with it / he is comfortable with it
So it teaches us (the actual lesson)

steps.whyThisMatters: A good purpose like a מצוה does not give a borrower the right to decide for the owner how his property is used.

phrases.english: It was necessary for him to mention a Torah scroll,
phrases.notes: "Him" means the תנא of the ברייתא. He is answering why the ספר תורה case had to be spelled out.

phrases.english: lest you say:
a person is pleased
to have a מצוה done with his property,
so it teaches us.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא נִיחָא לֵיהּ לְאִינִישׁ דְּתִיעֲבִיד מִצְוָה בְּמָמוֹנֵיהּ קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 18 about why the ברייתא repeats ריש לקיש's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why a case that seems unnecessary had to be stated (מהו דתימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because a ספר תורה is used for a מצוה, the owner would agree to it being lent on.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even a ספר תורה may not be lent out by the borrower.

steps.title: Isn't it obvious that a borrower may read the scroll?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the borrower may open and read the ספר תורה. The גמרא asks why this needs saying, since reading is the whole reason he borrowed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא says: he may open it and read it. Isn't that obvious? Why else would he have borrowed it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא and asks why it was needed. Reading is the whole point of borrowing a ספר תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא expects every line of a ברייתא to teach something new. Saying "he may read it" seems to add nothing, because nobody borrows a ספר תורה except to read it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (a challenge that a statement adds nothing)
He opens it and reads from it

phrases.english: He may open it and read it.
phrases.notes: This is the next line of the ברייתא from step 15, quoted again so the גמרא can ask about it.

phrases.english: That is obvious!
For what else did he borrow it from him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the same ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement "פותחו וקורא בו" about a borrowed ספר תורה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reading is the obvious purpose of borrowing a scroll, so stating that it is allowed seems pointless.

steps.title: The real point is the limit on reading
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא mentions reading only to set up the limit that follows: the borrower may not use the scroll to study new material for the first time.
steps.simpleTranslation: The last part of the line is what was needed: provided that he does not study something in it for the first time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא said "he may read" only as a lead-in to the limit that comes right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading is allowed, but studying a new section for the first time is not. A first-time learner keeps the scroll open for a long time, which can wear it out. So the new lesson is in the ending clause, not in the permission to read.

keyTerms.meaning: The last clause (end part of a teaching)

phrases.english: The last clause was what he needed:
provided that he does not study in it for the first time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא question in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The obvious part is stated only as a setup for the new part that follows it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The clause "he may read it" teaches nothing new.
steps.terutzMaskana: The clause is there to introduce the limit: reading is allowed, but not studying new material for the first time.

steps.title: Why may a guardian read the scroll at all?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says a guardian rolls a deposited ספר תורה and may open and read it. The גמרא asks two questions: what right does a guardian have to use it, and doesn't the ברייתא itself forbid opening it for his own use?
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא says: likewise, one who deposits a ספר תורה with his friend, the friend rolls it every twelve months, and he may open it and read it. What business does he have with it? And furthermore, the ברייתא says that if he opened it for himself it is forbidden, yet you said he may open it and read it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's section about a guardian of a ספר תורה and raises two problems with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First problem: a guardian is only supposed to keep the scroll safe, not use it, so why may he read it? Second problem: the same ברייתא later forbids opening it for his own sake, which seems to contradict the permission to read.

keyTerms.meaning: One who deposits an item with someone else for safekeeping
He rolls it (to air out the parchment)
What business does he have with it?

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הַמַּפְקִיד סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה אֵצֶל חֲבֵירוֹ –
phrases.english: And likewise, one who deposits a Torah scroll with his friend:
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא from step 16, quoted again here so the גמרא can ask about it.

phrases.english: he rolls it every twelve months,
he may open it and read it.
What business does he have with it?
And furthermore,
it says: if he opened it for himself, it is forbidden,
but you said: he may open it and read it!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי עֲבִידְתֵּיהּ גַּבֵּיהּ וְתוּ אִם בִּשְׁבִילוֹ פְּתָחוֹ אָסוּר הָא אָמְרַתְּ פּוֹתְחוֹ וְקוֹרֵא בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the borrower's section of the ברייתא to the guardian's section.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's permission for a guardian to open and read a deposited ספר תורה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A guardian has no right to use what he is guarding, and the ברייתא itself forbids opening it for his own sake, so it seems to contradict itself.

steps.title: Reading while rolling is allowed, opening just to read is not
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means that if the guardian reads while he is already rolling the scroll to care for it, that is allowed. Opening it only to read for himself is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the ברייתא means: if he opens and reads it while he is rolling it, it is permitted. If he opened it only for himself, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers both problems at once by explaining what the ברייתא really meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two rules are about two different situations, so they do not contradict each other. Reading during the rolling he must do anyway costs the owner nothing. Opening it just for his own learning is using someone else's property, which a guardian may not do.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he is saying (a reinterpretation)

steps.whatToRemember: A guardian of a ספר תורה may read it only while rolling it for its care. He may never open it just for his own use.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
if, while he is rolling it,
he opens it and reads it, it is permitted;
if he opened it for himself, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר אִם כְּשֶׁהוּא גּוֹלְלוֹ פּוֹתְחוֹ וְקוֹרֵא בּוֹ מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers both problems raised in step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation (הכי קאמר): the two rules apply to two different situations
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The guardian may open and read the scroll freely, which contradicts the ban on opening it for himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: Reading is allowed only during the rolling that is needed to care for the scroll. Opening it for his own sake is forbidden.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב seems to repeat the תנא קמא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא quotes סומכוס (new scroll every thirty days, old scroll every twelve months) and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב (both every twelve months). The גמרא objects that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב then says the same thing as the תנא קמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: סומכוס says: a new scroll is rolled every thirty days, an old one every twelve months. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: both are rolled every twelve months. But then רבי אליעזר בן יעקב is the same as the תנא קמא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the end of the ברייתא and points out that, as written, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב adds nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא already said every scroll is rolled every twelve months, with no difference between new and old. If רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says "both, twelve months," his view is identical. Why would the ברייתא list him as a separate opinion?

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: Sumakhos says:
phrases.notes: This is the same ברייתא text from step 17, quoted again so the גמרא can question it.

phrases.english: for a new one, thirty days;
for an old one, twelve months.
Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה – שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ.
phrases.english: both this one and that one, twelve months.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב, הַיְינוּ תַּנָּא קַמָּא!
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov is the same as the first tanna!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב הַיְינוּ תַּנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the last part of the ברייתא, the disagreement about how often to roll the scroll.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's opinion in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A named opinion that says exactly what the תנא קמא said is pointless, so the wording must be wrong.

steps.title: Correcting רבי אליעזר בן יעקב to thirty days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the text: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב actually says both new and old scrolls are rolled every thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says both this one and that one are rolled every thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of the ברייתא so that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב has his own separate view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are three distinct views. The תנא קמא says every scroll is rolled every twelve months. סומכוס says a new scroll every thirty days and an old one every twelve months. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says every scroll is rolled every thirty days.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this one and that one

steps.whatToRemember: Three views on rolling a deposited ספר תורה: תנא קמא, every twelve months; סומכוס, new every thirty days and old every twelve months; רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, every thirty days.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not use the earlier wording of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב (twelve months). After the גמרא's correction, his opinion is thirty days for every scroll.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם.
phrases.english: both this one and that one, thirty days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem in step 24 by correcting the text.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says twelve months for both kinds of scroll.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says thirty days for both kinds of scroll.

steps.title: May two people read one borrowed scroll together?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the rule that another person may not read along with the one holding the scroll. A ברייתא forbids only three readers, which implies that two are allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: he may not study something new in it, and another person may not read with him. But a ברייתא says: he may not read a passage and then review it, or read a passage and translate it, or open it more than three columns, and three people may not read from one volume. That implies two people may read!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה and points out that a ברייתא seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbids even a second reader. The ברייתא only forbids three readers in one volume, so it seems that two would be fine. The two sources look like they disagree about two readers.

keyTerms.meaning: And they set it against: the גמרא brings a source that seems to contradict
Review it, go over it again

phrases.english: But he shall not study in it for the first time
and another person shall not read with him.
And they raised a contradiction:
He shall not read a passage and then review it,
and he shall not read a passage in it and translate it,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא יִפְתַּח בּוֹ יוֹתֵר מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה דַּפִּין,
phrases.english: and he shall not open it more than three columns,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא יִקְרְאוּ בּוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה בְּנֵי אָדָם
phrases.english: and three people shall not read in it
from one volume –
which implies that two may read!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the rules about caring for someone else's ספר and starts a new contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that another person may not read along with the one holding someone else's scroll.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids only three readers, so it implies that two may read. That clashes with the משנה.

steps.title: Same passage versus different passages
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the ברייתא allows two readers who read the same passage. The משנה forbids two readers who read different passages.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is not difficult. Here, they are reading one subject. There, they are reading two different subjects.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי settles the contradiction by explaining that each source is talking about a different situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When two people read the same passage, each one follows where the other is, so they do not tug at the scroll. When each reads something different, they may pull the scroll back and forth and damage it. That is why the משנה forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the two sources do not really clash
A subject or passage being read

steps.whatToRemember: Two people may share a ספר that belongs to someone else only if they read the same passage together.

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is not difficult.
Here, when they read one subject,
phrases.notes: "Here" is the ברייתא, which allows two readers.

phrases.english: there, when they read two subjects.
phrases.notes: "There" is the משנה, which forbids two readers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source deals with a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא disagree about two readers.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two readers are allowed when they read the same passage and forbidden when they read different passages.

steps.title: Is shaking out a garment good or bad for it?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a finder shakes out a found garment once every thirty days. רבי יוחנן's statement suggests that shaking damages clothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: if he found a garment, he shakes it out once every thirty days. Does that mean shaking is good for it? But רבי יוחנן said: only someone who has a skilled weaver in his house should shake his garment every day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule about a found garment and challenges it with a statement of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats shaking as a way to look after the garment. רבי יוחנן implies that shaking wears clothing out, since only someone who can easily get new clothes from a weaver can afford to shake his garments. So how can the משנה ask the finder to shake it?
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not recommending shaking every day. He means it ruins clothes, so only someone with a weaver at home to replace them can afford it.

phrases.english: If he found a garment
he shakes it out once every thirty days.
Is this to say that shaking is good for it?
But didn't Rabbi Yoḥanan say:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ גַּרְדִּי אוּמָּן בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ,
phrases.english: One who has a skilled weaver in his house
may shake his garment every day!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּנִיעוּר מְעַלֵּי לַהּ? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה, about a found garment.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's instruction to shake out a found garment.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן implies that shaking damages clothing, so the משנה should not require it.

steps.title: Every day harms, once a month helps
steps.stepSummary: Shaking a garment every day damages it, but shaking it once in thirty days is good for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: shaking it every day is bad for it; shaking it once in thirty days is good for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that how often you shake the garment makes the difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן was talking about shaking every day, which wears the garment out. The משנה requires shaking only once a month, and that much actually helps the garment.

phrases.english: They say:
every day – it is harmful to it,
once in thirty days – it is good for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by how often the garment is shaken.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Shaking is always harmful, as רבי יוחנן seemed to say.
steps.terutzMaskana: Daily shaking harms the garment; monthly shaking helps it.

steps.title: One person versus two people shaking
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: shaking by one person helps the garment, while shaking by two people damages it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say instead: it is not difficult. This (the משנה) is when one person shakes it, and that (רבי יוחנן) is when two people shake it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer to the same challenge. The difference is how many people shake the garment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer is not about how often the garment is shaken. It is about who does the shaking. The משנה means one person shaking it, which helps. רבי יוחנן was talking about two people shaking it, which harms it.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say: brings in another possible answer
With one person / with two people

steps.whatToRemember: This is a second way to settle the garment question: one person versus two people shaking. Two more answers follow in the next steps.

phrases.english: If you wish, say: it is not difficult;
this is with one person,
phrases.notes: "This" is the משנה, which says shaking is good for the garment.

phrases.english: and that is with two.
phrases.notes: "That" is רבי יוחנן's case, where shaking does damage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the challenge from step 28, in place of step 29's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by how many people shake the garment.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The only way to settle the clash is by how often the garment is shaken.
steps.terutzMaskana: Shaking by one person helps; shaking by two people harms.

steps.title: Shaking by hand helps, shaking with a stick damages
steps.stepSummary: A third answer: the משנה means shaking a garment by hand, which is good for it. רבי יוחנן means beating it with a stick, which damages it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it is not a contradiction: this (the משנה) is shaking by hand, and that (רבי יוחנן) is beating with a stick.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another way to settle the clash between the משנה and רבי יוחנן about shaking a garment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answers split the cases by how often the garment is shaken and by how many people shake it. This answer splits them by what is used to shake it. A hand is gentle and helps the garment, while a stick is rough and damages it.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say; it introduces another possible answer

phrases.english: If you want, say: it is not difficult:
this is by hand,
phrases.notes: "This" is the משנה, where shaking out the garment is good for it.

phrases.english: and that is with a stick.
phrases.notes: "That" is רבי יוחנן's statement that shaking damages clothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third alternative answer to the קשיא in step 28
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by the method of shaking
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and רבי יוחנן seem to disagree about whether shaking is good or harmful.
steps.terutzMaskana: Shaking by hand helps the garment. Beating it with a stick damages it.

steps.title: Shaking helps wool but damages linen
steps.stepSummary: A fourth answer: the משנה is talking about a wool garment, which shaking helps. רבי יוחנן is talking about a linen garment, which shaking damages.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it is not a contradiction: this (the משנה) is about wool, and that (רבי יוחנן) is about linen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one more answer to the same contradiction, this time based on the fabric of the garment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the difference is not how the garment is shaken but what it is made of. Wool benefits from shaking, but linen is harmed by it. So each source is talking about a different fabric, and there is no contradiction.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא gives four ways to settle the shaking question: daily versus every thirty days, one person versus two, by hand versus with a stick, and wool versus linen.

phrases.english: If you want, say: it is not difficult:
this is about one of wool,
that is about one of linen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth alternative answer to the same קשיא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by type of fabric
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Shaking seems to be either always good or always harmful.
steps.terutzMaskana: Shaking is good for wool and harmful for linen.

steps.title: Lukewarm water is worse than a witch's cup
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that lukewarm water is so unhealthy that drinking from a witch's cup would be better.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Better a cup of witches than a cup of lukewarm water.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רבי יוחנן was just quoted, the גמרא brings another piece of his practical advice, this time about health.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This starts a new topic connected only because it comes from the same speaker. רבי יוחנן exaggerates on purpose to show how harmful lukewarm water is. Even a dangerous witch's drink would be a better choice.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
a cup of witches
phrases.notes: He means it is better to drink even a witch's drink.

phrases.english: and not a cup of lukewarm water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic linked by having the same speaker, רבי יוחנן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lukewarm water is extremely unhealthy to drink.

steps.title: Three limits on the lukewarm water warning
steps.stepSummary: The warning applies only to water in metal vessels, only when it was not boiled, and only when no flavorings were added.
steps.simpleTranslation: We said this only about metal vessels, but with earthenware vessels there is no problem. Even with metal vessels, we said this only when the water was not boiled. If it was boiled, there is no problem. And we said this only when no flavorings were put in. If flavorings were put in, there is no problem.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows רבי יוחנן's warning step by step, so it applies only in a small set of cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each "ולא אמרן אלא" removes a group of cases from the warning. Water in earthenware is fine. Metal-vessel water that was boiled is fine. Water with flavorings added is fine. The danger is only unboiled, unflavored lukewarm water in a metal vessel.

keyTerms.meaning: We said this only; it introduces a limit on the rule
We have no problem with it

steps.whatToRemember: Lukewarm water is a problem only when all three are true: it is in a metal vessel, it was not boiled, and no flavorings were added.

phrases.english: And we said this only about metal vessels.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בִּכְלֵי חֶרֶשׂ – לֵית לַן בַּהּ.
phrases.english: But with earthenware vessels, we have no problem with it.
And even with metal vessels,
we said this only when it was not boiled,
but when it was boiled, we have no problem with it.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא שְׁדָא בַּהּ צִיבַיָּא,
phrases.english: And we said this only when he did not put flavorings in it,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל שְׁדָא בֵּיהּ צִיבַיָּא – לֵית לַן בַּהּ.
phrases.english: but if he put flavorings in it, we have no problem with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the warning given in step 33
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The danger applies only to unboiled, unflavored lukewarm water in metal vessels.

steps.title: How to waste a large inheritance
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן lists three ways a person who wants to lose his inheritance can do it: wear linen, use glass, and hire workers without watching them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: Someone whose father left him a lot of money and wants to lose it should wear linen clothes, use glass vessels, and hire workers and not sit with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another practical teaching from רבי יוחנן, this time about wasting money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is advice given in reverse. Each item is a habit that slowly drains money: clothing that wears out fast, dishes that break easily, and workers nobody supervises. The real message is to avoid these habits.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁהִנִּיחַ לוֹ אָבִיו מָעוֹת הַרְבֵּה
phrases.english: one whose father left him a lot of money
and he wants to lose it,
should wear linen clothes,
and should use glass vessels,
and should hire workers and not sit with them.
phrases.notes: Not sitting with them means not staying to watch over their work.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִי שֶׁהִנִּיחַ לוֹ אָבִיו מָעוֹת הַרְבֵּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching from the same speaker, רבי יוחנן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Linen clothes, glass vessels, and unsupervised workers waste a person's money.

steps.title: Which linen, which glass, and what not watching workers means
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains each item: the linen is Roman linen, the glass is white glass, and it begins explaining the workers.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Wear linen clothes" means Roman linen. "Use glass vessels" means white glass. "Hire workers and not sit with them" is explained as follows:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back over רבי יוחנן's list to say exactly what each item means. The explanation of the workers continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not all linen or glass wastes money, only specific kinds. Roman linen wears out quickly, and white glass is expensive and breaks. The word "תרגומא" opens the explanation of the third item, which is given next.

keyTerms.meaning: Its explanation is; it introduces an explanation

phrases.english: He should wear linen garments:
this is about Roman linen.
And he should use glass vessels:
this is about white glass.
And he should hire workers and not sit with them:
its explanation is

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the items in רבי יוחנן's list from step 35
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The linen is Roman linen and the glass is white glass. The explanation of the workers continues next.
